description: The Ephemeris Expositors team by ASTRO Horizon is a student led scientific innovation team establishing new frontiers of space exploration through computational astronomy, astronomical data interpretation and orbital mechanics. its work focuses on transforming complex astronomical observations into accessible scientific investigations.
summary:
This project aims at mapping out points in our solar system with relatively high densities of abandoned equipment, bringing to light how there still lies abundant significance by visual aids tailored towards game development and promoting the ideology of “formal education is not the only means of education that should perpetually receive top priority” as a young space enthusiast can also obtain knowledge from practising familiar activities they actually enjoy while simultaneously assimilating knowledge and essential skills for navigative prowess in the world of space technology. 
In the native english language, the term ‘sentinel’ refers to one who (or that which) bears the burden of looking out for danger and preventing it (alias: watchman). It is historically evident that there is a dense population of space debris in the immediate cosmos and most people describe it as that which diminishes humanity’s welfare. A large portion of this space debris is discarded NASA equipment and this begs the question, is all discarded NASA hardware really apparently ‘useless’? 
Our team argues that this silent celestial hardware watches over us by observing the darkness’ unfoldings that humanity cannot comprehend.
details:
What the CSSO is about

The Celestial Silent Sentinels Observatory is a user-friendly interactive tool with the core purpose of correcting the information failure targeted mainly to the younger space enthusiasts regarding NASA discarded equipment on the moon, mars and across the solar system as a whole. If features for main gameplay modes;

Mode 01: Free Exploration (The Open Cosmos)

In this mode, players take the pilot’s seat to navigate an accurate 3D scale model of the solar system powered by real NASA/JPL planetary ephemerides and Keplerian orbital data. Instead of letting historic spacecraft fade into cosmic obscurity, the interactive observatory pinpoints the actual orbital coordinates and landing coordinates of more than 40 silent probes, satellites, and landers across space. By selecting targets like Voyager 1, Pioneer, or Hubble, players pull live telemetry and historical records directly from NASA's mission archives. This transforms forgotten hardware from invisible space debris into enduring, reachable monuments of human exploration.

Mode 02: Salvage (Abandoned, Not Forgotten)

Players command the salvage vessel Archive on an active recovery expedition across the rugged surfaces of the Moon, Mars, and Mercury. Guided by proximity sensor pings, players locate scattered wreckage components from historic missions, including the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Mars Pathfinder's Sojourner rover, and the MESSENGER Mercury orbiter. Assembling five critical modules on each celestial body reconstructs each forgotten machine while unlocking technical dossiers on its pioneering engineering achievements. It directly reflects the challenge's theme by demonstrating that every abandoned machine laid the indispensable technological groundwork for modern deep-space missions.

Mode 03: ISS Recovery (The Last Astronaut)

Framed as an alternate-history survival narrative, this mode places the player aboard an abandoned International Space Station nearing orbital decay with draining life-support reserves. To build a functioning return capsule back to Earth, the player must chart interplanetary trajectories to scavenge compatible spare parts left behind at historic exploration sites, including Apollo 11's guidance optics, Apollo 15's power regulator, and Opportunity and InSight's Martian avionics. Rather than portraying decommissioned hardware as useless junk, the gameplay turns legacy NASA engineering into humanity's sole lifeline home. It reminds players that early space tech was built with extraordinary durability and remains relevant even decades after mission shutdown.

Mode 04: NASA Startrail Odyssey (The Last Signal)

This story-driven surface adventure follows stranded astronaut Bob across authentic 3D NASA landing terrain mapped with Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and Mars Viking orbiter data. Exploring real heritage sites from the Apollo descent stages to the silent Opportunity rover players uncover memory logs, scientific instruments, and radio remnants left in the regolith. By blending real NASA 3D models with narrative reflection, the mission evokes the profound isolation of human artifacts resting beneath foreign skies. It honors the silent sentinels of space exploration, celebrating their enduring scientific legacy long after their primary transmitters went dark.
